sections.heading: Devnet 7 Chaos Testing Plans
sections.body:
- Grandine asked when more chaos testing (blob spamming, etc.) will begin on devnet 7, noting the network is stabilizing and it is a good time to try to break it again.
- Parithosh confirmed that chaos testing is planned for this week, pending Aussie team members merging PRs for the malicious CL client.
  - Basic spamming can start immediately after the call.
- The 300 million gas limit has not been tested on devnet 7 yet; Parithosh will add it to the testing plan.
- Payloads with more than 8,192 deposits have not been submitted on the devnet yet; Parithosh will do that as well.
- Blob limit on devnet 7 is unchanged from mainnet (21).

sections.heading: Malicious Prysm Node vs Death Star
sections.body:
- The malicious Prysm node differs from Death Star by working alongside a malicious orchestrator and a builder.
  - The orchestrator has a global view of what both the builder and the Prysm node are doing, enabling coordinated edge-case creation (e.g., builder releasing payload late while proposer withholds blobs).
- Death Star covers basic malformed payloads and similar scenarios.
- Nico (Lodestar / Death Star) has additional features planned; coordination needed with the malicious Prysm team on who implements what.
  - Some scenarios require a proposer role; a proposer can technically do everything without a separate builder, but testing builder paths is important since builders can always be malicious.

sections.heading: Devnet 8 and Testnet Timeline
sections.body:
- Devnet 8 is targeted as a large, public-ish devnet approximately 2 weeks out (first week of August).
  - Goal: invite contract developers and others to deploy and try to break things.
  - Roughly 2 weeks after launch to process data and finalize repricing numbers.
- A parallel non-finality devnet is planned, covering 3–4 non-finality scenarios plus one potential decoupled consensus test.
- Parithosh's ideal for testnet upgrades is September, contingent on findings during the next month of devnet testing.
- By devnet 8 completion, all standard testing categories (malicious proposals, basic fuzzing, benchmarking, non-finality) should be covered.

sections.heading: Builder API and Direct Connection Specs
sections.body:
- Potuz stressed that the builder API flow — including signed authorizations, key manager API, and sidecar handling — must be tested well before testnets, noting 99% of mainnet blocks come through builders.
  - Falling back to the circuit breaker due to untested builder paths is undesirable.
- Key blocking spec PRs that must be reviewed and merged:
  - [beacon-APIs PR #625](https://github.com/ethereum/beacon-APIs/pull/625) — POST version of ProduceBlock (by Potuz; has merge conflicts after Nico's earlier PR merged)
  - [keymanager-APIs PR #87](https://github.com/ethereum/keymanager-APIs/pull/87) — builds on top of Potuz's beacon-APIs PR
  - A related [builder-specs commit](https://github.com/ethereum/builder-specs/commit/5078eabc63cf092007bb933ae16209087c053eba)
  - [beacon-APIs PR #627](https://github.com/ethereum/beacon-APIs/pull/627) — produceBlockV4 improvement by Luca (Vero), also related but not conflicting
- Prysm has a draft implementation but it is not yet merged; Teku is planning implementation (Stefan working on it); Lodestar has a draft PR (Nico) needing significant work.
- Terence emphasized that delaying the API merge risks it landing too late even for testnet; early review is critical.
- Parithosh asked if all these changes can target devnet 8 (~2 weeks); Teku was unsure of feasibility.
- Terence noted there were comments from the previous week on Potuz's PR awaiting Potuz's response.

sections.heading: Builder API Testing Coordination with MEV Ecosystem
sections.body:
- Justin asked whether PBS Foundation would support builder API testing.
- Terence noted that a biweekly MEV Boost Community Call is hosted by PBS Foundation; CommitBoost team is willing to help with testing, but all are waiting for the API to be finalized and merged.
- Justin and Terence both acknowledged they haven't attended those calls recently; Terence agreed to raise the topic there.
- Justin questioned whether the EF should be testing the external builder flow at all, suggesting builders themselves should test direct connections; Potuz and Terence pushed back, citing the 99% builder block share on mainnet.

sections.heading: Ahead-of-Time Builder Preferences
sections.body:
- Nico raised uncertainty around whether builder preferences should be sent ahead of time or just in time.
  - A few builders claimed they need ahead-of-time preferences, but could not clearly explain why on Discord.
- Nico favored simplifying the spec and avoiding complexity for features whose usefulness is uncertain.
- Dustin found Alex's comment (arguing for ahead-of-time preferences) unconvincing: the scenario involves a proposer changing their mind very late about accepting a category of bid, which Dustin viewed as the proposer's problem rather than a spec requirement.
- No resolution reached; topic remains open.

sections.heading: Fork-Choice Testing with Kurtosis
sections.body:
- Potuz is running Kurtosis fork-choice scenarios focused on how clients attest, testing all types of withholding including long reorgs and builder-proposer collusions.
  - Kurtosis preferred over devnet for this because peering is controlled and attestations can be tracked precisely.
- Results so far: with an even distribution of clients, collective behavior appears broadly correct.
  - However, unexplained stray attestations from random clients are being observed; Potuz cannot yet pinpoint the cause.
- Nico noted that analyzing attestation behavior on devnet 7 is complicated by honest reorgs due to genuinely late payloads, plus Death Star always reorging payloads and withholding PTC votes.
  - Fork-choice dumps from Death Star are available to aid analysis.
